wave64_cost_followup.decision: Keep the existing Q4 cost table. Updating it to current short-context draft-plus-verification costs loses 0.74% prose and 4.46% JSON despite preserved greedy AR tokens. The kernel improvements from 6654d1e remain retained.

profile_basis.method: Reuse final qualified 6654d1e prose profile (110 rounds) plus one new JSON profile (43 rounds, unchanged tokens and acceptance), same release. GPU trace wall spans are diagnostic, not unprofiled speed measurements.
profile_basis.candidate_rounding: Measured relative costs rounded to four decimal places.

paired_release_speed.method: Q4/Q4 C1 greedy. Updated offline Q4 controller cost curve compared against qualified 6654d1e release. Two samples per binary ABBA for raw prose/JSON TG300 warmup excluded. All IDs checked against qualified AR references; controller history may change, acceptance must replay within each binary; prefill included, load excluded. Only the offline controller cost constants change. Target and draft arithmetic, proposal sampling and verification stay unchanged.

wave64_cost_followup.interpretation: A cheaper wide verifier does not guarantee faster adaptive decoding. The new table drafts 509 instead of 476 prose tokens without reducing its 110 rounds. JSON drafts 302 instead of 285, accepts 254 instead of 256 and takes 45 instead of 43 rounds. These measured sequences invalidate a speed prediction based on verification costs alone; they do not establish a sampler correctness problem.
limits: C1 Q4 target/Q4 draft, short raw prose and JSON TG300 only; no new depth, capability or C>1 sweep.
